clue.text: Spot for revealing thong in front of group?

indicators.note: says the first piece comes before the second in the grid

parts.note: a thong is a narrow strip of leather
a club is a group of members

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about where a thong might be on show ahead of a band or gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thong' looks like underwear, which suits the surface, but here it is a leather strip.
explanation.definitionFit: A venue where performers undress is literally a place for revealing, hence the whimsical description.

clue.text: One son wearing pair of smalls close to lady, getting wet

indicators.note: the pieces for one and son sit inside the pair of letters, as if wearing them

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, so a pair is two of them
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, here of lady

explanation.surface: A boy in his underwear beside a woman, getting soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smalls' is British slang for underwear, but here means two small sizes.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet in British slang describes a feeble, timid person, a weakling.

clue.text: Now powerful outrage upset conservationists

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word for outrage upside down

parts.note: anger is outrage
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage conservation charity

explanation.surface: Environmental campaigners angry about something are now a force to reckon with.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes someone currently reigning, holding power at present.

clue.text: Pull up grass here?

definitions.meaning: to stop a car and leave it at the roadside
a public green space where grass grows

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to pull up the weeds in this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means stopping a vehicle and leaving it; the noun is a public green space.

clue.text: Live wire

definitions.meaning: to ... a life is to live it

explanation.surface: A live wire, an energetic person or a dangerous cable.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb sense is living a particular life; the noun is an electrical flex.

clue.text: Singers need pieces of 15 to cover live Adele hit?

indicators.note: the bar piece goes round the rest, covering it

parts.note: 15 is the across answer meaning score; its pieces are bars
L marks the live terminal on a British plug

indicators.note: hit, like struck, means knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: Singers covering an Adele hit live need sheet music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' looks like a chart success but is the anagram signal; 'cover' looks like a cover version.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballad singers are singers of a particular kind, so the plural names performers.

clue.text: Breaks sculptures

definitions.meaning: smashes or breaks open, as a raid breaks a ring
carved heads and shoulders on plinths

explanation.surface: Someone smashes statues.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is to break or smash; the noun is a sculpted head and shoulders.

clue.text: Drink by mayor and old drunk

indicators.note: a drunk mixture is unsteady, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drink consumed by the mayor and an old drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of vodka and tomato juice, a well-known mixed drink.

clue.text: Insects regularly suck on horses

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of suck

parts.note: Arabs are a breed of horse

explanation.surface: Insects keep feeding on horses.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarabs are dung beetles, sacred in ancient Egypt, so are insects.

clue.text: Party with thrills for partners

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute
kicks are thrills

explanation.surface: A party with excitement for couples.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidekicks are companions or assistants, partners in some enterprise.

clue.text: Ring man once your lad arranges supply

indicators.note: read as the adverb of supple, bending these letters into a new shape

explanation.surface: A young man is told he sorts out the provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranges' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'supply', meaning in a supple way, does the job.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a celebrated American boxer of the 1980s, a man of the boxing ring who has now retired.

clue.text: Short story gripping English student group

indicators.note: gripping says one piece holds another inside it
short says the word for story loses its last letter

parts.note: a yarn is a tall story

explanation.surface: A brief tale holds the attention of a class of students learning English.
explanation.definitionFit: Schools sort pupils into cohorts by age, so a single cohort such as Year Nine is a group of students.

clue.text: With model after love at first sight

indicators.note: says the pieces for with and model come after that letter
at first takes only the opening letter of the word love

parts.note: and means together with
a mark is a model or version, as in Mark II

explanation.surface: Echoes love at first sight, with a model thrown in.
explanation.definitionFit: A prominent feature, a famous building or monument, is one of the sights a visitor goes to see.

clue.text: Do specify books for competition

parts.note: to do a country is to tour it as a visitor
to name is to specify
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Instructions for entering a contest: choose some books.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournament is a sporting contest made up of many matches.

clue.text: Rock star beds her, ignoring top birds

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so the letters are shaken up
ignoring the top, in a down clue the first letter, of the word her

explanation.surface: A rock star seduces a woman, ignoring something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like part of 'rock star' but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Robins are traditionally called this, from their red chests, so these are birds.

clue.text: Move back in June — decor terrible, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone reflects that the decoration chosen in June was awful and wants to back out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters hidden in the words that follow; 'on reflection' reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: This rare verb means to go back or recede, from the Latin for retreating.

clue.text: They give information for meeting people: funny people!

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
a card is a joker, an amusing person

explanation.surface: Something helps you meet people, some of them funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meeting' is a horse-race meeting, not people meeting each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed programmes list the runners and riders at a horse-race meeting.

clue.text: Score as recorded, following header from Man United

indicators.note: says the last piece comes after the others
the header from a word is its first letter, here of Man

parts.note: U is the standard abbreviation for United in team names
sic is Latin for thus, printed to show a word is as written in the source

explanation.surface: A football score as reported, after an early goal from a Manchester United player.
explanation.walkthrough: Man United is the everyday name for Manchester United football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is the written music for a piece, so the two words can stand for each other.

clue.text: Wood in church needing a lot of repair

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

indicators.note: a lot of, but not all, so the word for repair loses its last letter

parts.note: to darn is to repair a hole in cloth

explanation.surface: Woodwork in a church that needs a great deal of fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: This conifer gives a fragrant timber, so it names a type of wood.

clue.text: Moon was one day on right: no sun in season

indicators.note: no says the letter for sun is taken away from the season word

parts.note: summer is a season
S is the abbreviation for sun or Sunday

explanation.surface: An astronomy note: the moon was in position one day, and no sun shone in summer.
explanation.walkthrough: Keith Moon played percussion for The Who.
explanation.definitionFit: Keith Moon was the percussionist of the rock band The Who.

clue.text: Plots mum and dad start to rake with interest in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going backwards, so the whole run is read in reverse

parts.note: keeping mum means keeping quiet, and sh is the call for quiet
pa is a familiar name for dad

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, here of rake

parts.note: to grab someone is to interest them

explanation.surface: Mum and dad scheme to start raking it in from interest after they retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is not a mother here but the word for silence.
explanation.definitionFit: Charts with bars of varying height are plots of data, the word plots meaning graphs here.

clue.text: I don't know Basic code

parts.note: saying pass in a quiz means not knowing the answer
key means fundamental, basic

explanation.surface: Someone confesses ignorance of the computer language BASIC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Basic' looks like the programming language, but means fundamental.
explanation.definitionFit: A password or entry code that opens a lock or system.

clue.text: Caught opening pair for Australia out with tail

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the opening pair of a word is its first two letters, here of Australia

parts.note: out of fashion means dated

explanation.surface: A cricket report: an Australian opener caught, and the tail exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the opening pair are the first two batsmen and the tail is the weak lower order.
explanation.definitionFit: A zoological adjective from the Latin cauda, meaning having a tail.

clue.text: Quickly like a post at the beginning

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of

indicators.note: takes only the opening letter of the word post

explanation.surface: Something resembling a fence post placed at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbreviation for as soon as possible, meaning without delay.

clue.text: Number one across North Carolina and number two in Washington

indicators.note: the first piece stretches across the second, holding it inside

parts.note: number one is a childish word for urinating, pee
NC is the abbreviation for the US state of North Carolina

explanation.surface: Rankings of US states and capital: number one to number two.
explanation.walkthrough: Mike Pence was then US Vice President, the second in command in Washington.
explanation.definitionFit: Mike Pence was Vice President when this was set, second only to the President.

clue.text: Girl lives in city

indicators.note: says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
is means exists, lives

explanation.surface: A young woman lives in a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisa is a common female first name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Issue with looker left out of Vogue

indicators.note: says the letter for left is taken out

parts.note: style is vogue, fashion

explanation.surface: A problem with a model left out of the fashion magazine Vogue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looker' looks like a pretty model but is an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a problem with the eye.

clue.text: First to read new Little Miss Punk children's book

indicators.note: the first letter of the word read
something new is made over, so these letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: A new title in the Little Miss series, about a punk girl, should be read first.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Miss books are a popular series of children's picture books.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grimm fairy tale of the name-guessing imp is published as a picture book for youngsters.

clue.text: Rod Stewart's gutted with track

indicators.note: something gutted loses its insides, leaving only the outside letters of Stewart

parts.note: a rut is a groove or track

explanation.surface: The singer Rod Stewart is devastated by a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like the singer's first name but is the definition; ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar or rod used as a brace in a framework is a strut.

clue.text: Thin buttery layer, essentially on fatty roll

parts.note: spare means lean or thin

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its central letter, taken from buttery and from layer

parts.note: re means on, concerning

explanation.surface: A thin buttery layer spread on a fatty bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for a roll of fat round the waist, likened to a reserve wheel.
